questions.title: Hobby-X workshops, rusks recipe and bank interest rates

subQuestions.questionText: Hobby-X offers workshops where they teach art skills. The diameter of the cheeseboard is 300 mm. Calculate the radius of the cheeseboard.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Radius $= 300\ \text{mm} \div 2$ (1MA dividing by 2)
Mark 2: $= 150$ mm OR $15$ cm (1A simplification)

subQuestions.questionText: Write the cost of the 90-minute workshops in descending order. (90-minute workshops: Art for Beginners R330,00; Cheeseboard R110,00; Creative Hand Lettering R220,00; Creative Journaling R275,00.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Reading all four values (1RT)
Mark 2: R330,00; R275,00; R220,00; R110,00 (1CA correct descending order)

subQuestions.questionText: Determine the VAT amount charged for the Creative Journaling workshop. (Creative Journaling cost: R275,00 excluding 15% VAT.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Method 1:
Mark 1: VAT $= \text{R}275{,}00 \times 15\%$ (1MA multiplying by 15%)
Mark 2: $= \text{R}41{,}25$ (1A simplification)

OR Method 2:
Mark 1: Price including VAT $= 275 \times 1{,}15 = \text{R}316{,}25$ (1MA calculating VAT-inclusive price)
Mark 2: VAT $= 316{,}25 - 275 = \text{R}41{,}25$ (1A simplification)

subQuestions.questionText: Convert 150 minutes to hours.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: $150 \div 60$ (1A divide by 60)
Mark 2: $= 2{,}5$ hours OR $2\frac{1}{2}$ hours (1A 2,5 hours)

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate (excluding VAT) the total cost for a person attending all the workshops. (Costs: Art for Beginners R330; Bunny Bin R220; Cheeseboard R110; Chef's Breadbin R165; Creative Hand Lettering R220; Creative Journaling R275.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Total $= 330 + 275 + 220 + 220 + 165 + 110$ (1MA adding all correct values)
Mark 2: $= \text{R}1\,320$ (1MCA simplify — at least 5 correct values)

subQuestions.questionText: Determine the discount amount offered for the Art for Beginners' workshop. (First 10 participants in each workshop receive 7,5% discount; cost R330,00.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Discount $= \text{R}330{,}00 \times 7{,}5\%$ (1MA multiplying by 7,5%)
Mark 2: $= \text{R}24{,}75$ (1A simplification)

subQuestions.questionText: Naomi bakes rusks. The recipe (4 000 g of rusks) requires 1 250 g of self-raising flour. Convert 1 250 grams (g) to kilograms (kg).
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: $\frac{1\,250\ \text{g}}{1\,000}$ (1MA dividing by 1 000)
Mark 2: $= 1{,}25$ kg (1A simplification)

subQuestions.questionText: Determine the cost price of a 500 g pack if a profit of R30,30 per pack was made. (Selling price = R55,00 per pack.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Cost price $= \text{R}55{,}00 - \text{R}30{,}30$ (1MA subtracting correct values in correct order)
Mark 2: $= \text{R}24{,}70$ (1A simplification)

subQuestions.questionText: Write (in simplified form) the ratio of self-raising flour to butter. (Self-raising flour: 1 250 g; Butter: 500 g.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: $1\,250 : 500$ (1MA values in correct order)
Mark 2: $= 5 : 2$ OR $2{,}5 : 1$ OR $1 : 0{,}4$ (1CA simplified form)

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the mass of raisins or dates needed to bake a 500 g pack of rusks. (The recipe makes 4 000 g of rusks using 100 g of raisins or dates.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Method 1:
Mark 1: Number of 500 g packs $= \frac{4\,000}{500} = 8$ (1A number of 500 g packs)
Mark 2: Mass $= \frac{100\,\text{g}}{8}$ (1MA dividing 100 g by 8)
Mark 3: $= 12{,}5$ g (1CA simplification)

OR Method 2:
Mark 1: Mass $= \frac{500\,\text{g} \times 100\,\text{g}}{4\,000\,\text{g}}$ (1MA number of 500 g packs)
Mark 2: (1A dividing 4 000 g)
Mark 3: $= 12{,}5$ g (1CA simplification)

OR Method 3:
Mark 1: $4\,000\,\text{g} : 100\,\text{g} = 500\,\text{g} : x$ (1MA correct ratio concept)
Mark 2: Mass of raisins $= \frac{50\,000}{4\,000}$ (1A dividing 4 000 g)
Mark 3: $= 12{,}5$ g (1CA simplification)

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the number of cups of bran flour needed if Naomi bakes 8 000 g of rusks. (Recipe makes 4 000 g of rusks using 5 cups of bran flour.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Method 1:
Mark 1: $2 \times 5$ (1MA multiply by 2 and 5)
Mark 2: $= 10$ cups (1A simplification)

OR Method 2:
Mark 1: $4\,000 : 5 = 8\,000 : 10$ (1MA correct ratio)
Mark 2: Number of cups = 10 (1A simplification)

subQuestions.questionText: The tables represent the percentage interest that could be earned on savings at two different banks. Define the term interest in the given context.
subQuestions.memoText: Mark 1–2: Money earned on an investment (2A definition).

subQuestions.questionText: Write down the minimum number of months that Bank A offers an interest rate of 7,35%.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1–2: 25 months (2A correct number of months).
From Table 2: 7,35% applies to the 25–36 month range.

subQuestions.questionText: Name which bank offers the better interest rate for an amount of R145 000, invested for 2 years.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1–2: Bank A (2A correct bank).
Bank A offers 7,20% for 19–24 months at R100 000+, while Bank B offers 6,8% for the R100 000–R249 999 range.

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the difference between the highest interest rate of Bank A and the lowest interest rate of Bank B.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: 7,50% from Bank A (1RT correct value from table)
Mark 2: 6,7% from Bank B (1RT correct value from table)
Mark 3: $7{,}50\% - 6{,}7\% = 0{,}8\%$ (1CA simplification — one value must be correct)

questions.title: Dental quotation, vegetable garden break-even and exchange rates

subQuestions.questionText: ANNEXURE A shows a quotation for a dental procedure for Ms Mpho Hendricks. Write down the name of the dentist who is treating Mpho.
subQuestions.memoText: Mark 1–2: Dr. JJ Ndlovu (2A correct name).

subQuestions.questionText: (Refer to ANNEXURE A.) State the year in which Mpho was born.
subQuestions.memoText: Mark 1–2: 1982 / '82 (2RT reading from table).

subQuestions.questionText: (Refer to ANNEXURE A.) Write down the amount that Mpho has to pay when the procedure is done.
subQuestions.memoText: Mark 1–2: R0,00 / nothing (2A correct amount).

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the total amount excluding 15% VAT. (Total amount including VAT = R1 744,75.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Method 1:
Mark 1: $\frac{115}{100}$ OR $\frac{100}{115}$ (1A correct fraction)
Mark 2: $\text{R}1\,744{,}75 \div \frac{115}{100}$ OR $\times \frac{100}{115}$ (1M dividing or multiplying)
Mark 3: $= \text{R}1\,517{,}17$ (1CA simplification)

OR Method 2:
Mark 1: VAT amount $= \text{R}1\,744{,}75 \times \frac{15}{115} = \text{R}227{,}58$ (1A amount VAT)
Mark 2: $\text{R}1\,744{,}75 - \text{R}227{,}58$ (1M subtracting VAT)
Mark 3: $= \text{R}1\,517{,}17$ (1CA simplification)

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the price of ONE infection control measure. (Total for infection controls listed on quotation = R40,55 for 2.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: $\text{R}40{,}55 \div 2$ (1MA divide by 2)
Mark 2: $= \text{R}20{,}28$ (1A simplification)
NPR. AO (answer only acceptable).

subQuestions.questionText: Mpho's sister, Anelle, has a vegetable garden and sells mixed vegetable packs. Calculate Anelle's total monthly fixed cost. (Rent for stall: R140,00; Transport: R60,00.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: $\text{R}140{,}00 + \text{R}60{,}00$ (1RT correct values)
Mark 2: $= \text{R}200{,}00$ (1CA simplification — one value must be correct)

subQuestions.questionText: The formula Expenses (R) = 200,00 + 12,50 × number of packs is used to calculate Anelle's expenses for one month. From TABLE 6: when number of packs = 10, expenses = A; when expenses = R400, number of packs = B. Use the formula to calculate the missing values A and B.
subQuestions.memoText:
For A:
Mark 1: $A = 200 + 12{,}50 \times 10$ (1SF correct substitution)
Mark 2: $A = 200 + 125 = \text{R}325{,}00$ (1A simplification)

For B:
Mark 1: $B = 400 \div 25$ OR $B = (400 - 200) \div 12{,}5$ (1SF correct substitution)
Mark 2: $B = 16$ packs (1A simplification)
AO (answer only acceptable).

subQuestions.label: 2.2.3(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Use the same grid provided on the ANSWER SHEET to draw another line graph showing the income from the sale of the mixed vegetable packs. (Selling price = R25,00 per pack; income at 0 packs = R0; income at 50 packs = R1 250.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Starting point (0; 0) (1A starting point)
Mark 2: Endpoint (50; 1 250) (1A endpoint)
Mark 3: Straight line joining at least 3 points stated in the table (1A straight line — CA for using B from Q2.2.2)

subQuestions.label: 2.2.3(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Explain the meaning of the term break-even in the given context.
subQuestions.memoText: Mark 1–2: Where the cost price of the mixed vegetable packs equals the selling price of the packs (2A explanation).

subQuestions.label: 2.2.3(c)
subQuestions.questionText: Write down the number of mixed vegetable packs that must be sold to break even.
subQuestions.memoText:
(CA from Q2.2.2 / 2.2.3(a).)
Mark 1–2: 16 packs (2A correct number of packs).

subQuestions.label: 2.3.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Anelle is thinking of using Payment Option 2 (Deposit: 20% of cash price; 24 monthly payments of R95,00). Cash price = R1 799,00. Calculate the deposit amount she has to pay.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Deposit $= \text{R}1\,799{,}00 \times \frac{20}{100}$ (1MA calculating 20%)
Mark 2: $= \text{R}359{,}80$ (1A simplification)

subQuestions.label: 2.3.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Determine (rounded to the nearest rand) the total amount Anelle will have paid for the vegetable slicer after 24 months.
subQuestions.memoText:
(CA from Q2.3.1(a).)
Mark 1: $24 \times \text{R}95{,}00 = \text{R}2\,280{,}00$ (1MA multiplying by 24)
Mark 2: Total $= \text{R}359{,}80 + \text{R}2\,280{,}00$ (1MCA adding the deposit)
Mark 3: $= \text{R}2\,639{,}80$ (1CA simplification)
Mark 4: $\approx \text{R}2\,640{,}00$ (1R to the nearest rand)

subQuestions.label: 2.3.2(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Explain what the term exchange rate means.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: The value of one currency (1A value of one currency)
Mark 2: relative to the value of another currency (1A relative to the value of another currency)

subQuestions.label: 2.3.2(b)
subQuestions.questionText: (Refer to TABLE 7.) Identify the currency that is weaker than the rand.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1–2: Yen / ¥ OR Japanese yen (2A correct currency).
The yen is the only currency in the table where 1 ZAR equals more than 1 unit of the foreign currency (1 ZAR = 7,386276 yen).

subQuestions.label: 2.3.2(c)
subQuestions.questionText: Tony sent Anelle US\$130,00. Determine, rounded to the nearest rand, the amount Anelle received from Tony. (Use the exchange rate from TABLE 7: 1 ZAR = 0,067251 US\$ OR 1 US\$ = ZAR14,86966737.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Method 1:
Mark 1: 1 ZAR = \$0,067251 (1RT exchange rate)
Mark 2: $\frac{\$130}{\$0{,}067251} \times \text{R}1 = \text{R}1\,933{,}056758$ (1C conversion)
Mark 3: $\approx \text{R}1\,933{,}00$ (1R correct rounding)

OR Method 2:
Mark 1: \$1 = ZAR14,86966737 (1RT exchange rate)
Mark 2: $\$130 \times \text{R}14{,}86966737 = \text{R}1\,933{,}056758$ (1C conversion)
Mark 3: $\approx \text{R}1\,933{,}00$ (1R correct rounding)

questions.title: Candle making — packaging, ribbon, volume and probability

subQuestions.questionText: Simphiwe makes cylindrical candles (diameter 10,4 cm, height 11,4 cm). Simphiwe will pack 12 cylindrical candles in a box using a 4 by 3 arrangement. Determine the minimum length and width of the box he needs if the candles are tightly packed, touching each other in the box.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Width $= 3 \times 10{,}4$ cm (1MA for multiplying diameter by 3)
Mark 2: $= 31{,}2$ cm (1A simplification)
Mark 3: Length $= 4 \times 10{,}4$ cm (1MA for multiplying diameter by 4)
Mark 4: $= 41{,}6$ cm (1A simplification)

subQuestions.questionText: Simphiwe ties a decorative ribbon around the candles. The ribbon has an overlap of 3 cm. Determine the number of candles he will be able to decorate with a 20-metre long ribbon. (Use Ribbon needed for one candle (cm) $= 2 \times 3{,}142 \times \text{radius} + 3$. Candle radius = 5,2 cm.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Ribbon for 1 candle $= 2 \times 3{,}142 \times 5{,}2 + 3$ (1SF correct substitution — radius)
Mark 2: $= 35{,}6768$ cm (1A length for 1 candle)
Mark 3: $20 \times 100 = 2\,000$ cm (1C conversion)
Mark 4: Number of candles $= \frac{2\,000}{35{,}6768}$ (1MCA dividing by length of ribbon)
Mark 5: $= 56{,}05883936 \approx 56$ candles (1R correct number of candles)
[Accept 55 candles if rounded earlier.]

subQuestions.questionText: After carving a horsehead in a cylindrical candle, he collected the leftover wax, melted it and poured it in the mould. The leftover melted wax filled up $\frac{1}{3}$ of the mould. Calculate the volume of wax needed for one horsehead candle. (Use Volume of a cylinder $= 3{,}142 \times (\text{radius})^2 \times \text{height}$; radius = 5,2 cm; height = 11,4 cm.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Method 1:
Mark 1: Volume $= 3{,}142 \times (5{,}2)^2 \times 11{,}4$ (1SF substituting correct values)
Mark 2: $= 968{,}54\ \text{cm}^3$ (1CA answer in cm³)
Mark 3: Volume of horsehead $= \frac{2}{3} \times 968{,}54$ (1MCA multiply by 2 and dividing by 3)
Mark 4: $= 645{,}69\ \text{cm}^3$ (1CA simplification)

OR Method 2:
Volume $= 968{,}54\ \text{cm}^3$; $\frac{968{,}54}{3} = 322{,}84666 \times 2 = 645{,}69\ \text{cm}^3$.

OR Method 3 (subtraction):
Volume of horsehead $= 968{,}54 - \frac{1}{3}(968{,}54) = 968{,}54 - 322{,}85 = 645{,}69\ \text{cm}^3$.

subQuestions.label: 3.2.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText: (Refer to the tree diagram.) Write down the description for X. (X is the decoration for a black horsehead candle.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1–2: Ribbon / R (2A ribbon).
The outcome HBR (Horsehead, Black, Ribbon) requires X to be 'Ribbon'.

subQuestions.label: 3.2.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Write down the description for Y. (Y is the outcome for a black horsehead candle with no ribbon.)
subQuestions.memoText: Mark 1–2: HBN (2A HBN — Horsehead, Black, No ribbon).

subQuestions.label: 3.2.2(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Write down the probability of buying any candle with a ribbon, as a percentage.
subQuestions.memoText:
Method 1:
Mark 1: $\frac{1}{2}$ (1A fraction — 4 ribbon outcomes out of 8 total)
Mark 2: $\times 100\%$ (1M concept of percentage)
Mark 3: $= 50\%$ (1CA for percentage)

OR Method 2:
Mark 1: $\frac{4}{8}$ (1A fraction)
Mark 2: $\times 100\%$ (1M concept of percentage)
Mark 3: $= 50\%$ (1CA)
AO (answer only acceptable).

subQuestions.label: 3.2.2(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Write down the probability of buying a gold horsehead candle, without a ribbon.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1–2: P(Gold horsehead candle) $= 0$ OR Impossible OR $\frac{0}{8}$ OR $0\%$ OR $0{,}0$ (2A correct probability).
There is no gold horsehead in the tree diagram (horsehead candles only come in white or black).

questions.title: Map of Northern Cape and university layout plan

subQuestions.questionText: Alida is a Grade 12 learner who lives in Grootdrink in the Northern Cape and intends studying at a university in Bloemfontein. (Use ANNEXURE B.) Write down the general direction from Bloemfontein to Grootdrink.
subQuestions.memoText: Mark 1–2: North West / NW (2RT reading from map).

subQuestions.questionText: (Refer to ANNEXURE B.) State the national road they will use to travel to Bloemfontein.
subQuestions.memoText: Mark 1–2: N8 (2RT N8).

subQuestions.questionText: (Refer to ANNEXURE B.) Write down the name of the third town they will pass en route to Bloemfontein.
subQuestions.memoText: Mark 1–2: Campbell (2RT town).

subQuestions.questionText: Alida and her parents will leave Grootdrink at 04:00 to travel the distance of 496,9 km to Bloemfontein. Determine (to the nearest km/h) the average speed they must travel to be in Bloemfontein at 09:30. Use $\text{Average speed} = \frac{\text{distance}}{\text{time}}$.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: $09{:}30 - 04{:}00 = 5$ hours 30 min $= 5{,}5$ hours (1A calculating 5,5 hours)
Mark 2: Average speed $= \frac{496{,}9}{5{,}5}$ (1MCA dividing correct values in correct order)
Mark 3: $= 90{,}3454545$ km/h (1CA simplification)
Mark 4: $\approx 90$ km/h (1R rounding)

subQuestions.questionText: The layout plan of the ground floor of a university is given. SCALE = 1 : 380. Explain the meaning of the given scale.
subQuestions.memoText: Mark 1–2: 1 unit on the plan represents 380 units in real life (2A explanation).

subQuestions.questionText: Name a feature on the layout plan that indicates that this is a multi-level building.
subQuestions.memoText: Mark 1–2: Lifts OR Ground Floor OR Stairs (2A lifts).

subQuestions.questionText: Determine the number of toilets not suitable for people with disabilities on this layout plan.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1–2: 4 (2A correct value).
[Accept 2.]

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the entrance that will be closest to the cafe.
subQuestions.memoText: Mark 1–2: Bloed Street entrance OR South entrance (2RT correct entrance).

subQuestions.questionText: Measure (in mm) the east-facing wall of the Mindsphere Lounge.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1–2: 27 mm (2A for correct measurement)
Mark 3: Correct wall identified (1A correct wall)
[Accept 26 – 28 mm.]

questions.title: Statistics — level descriptors, frequency table and NSC subject candidates

subQuestions.questionText: In South Africa, learners' marks are graded using level descriptors from level 1 (L1), the lowest, to level 7 (L7), the highest. Define the term range.
subQuestions.memoText: Mark 1–2: Range is the difference between the highest/maximum value and the lowest/minimum value in a data set (2A correct definition).

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the type of graph shown.
subQuestions.memoText: Mark 1–2: Line graph OR Broken line graph (2A correct graph).

subQuestions.questionText: State whether the learner numbers represent continuous or discrete data.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1–2: Discrete data (2A discrete).
Learner numbers are countable whole numbers, so the data is discrete.

subQuestions.questionText: Determine the total number of Grade 10 learners who sat for the examinations. (Grade 10 values: L1 = 1 749; L2 = 2 239; L3 = 1 618; L4 = 903; L5 = 429; L6 = 150; L7 = 16.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Reading values $1\,749, 2\,239, 1\,618, 903, 429, 150, 16$ (1RT correct values)
Mark 2: Adding ALL values (1M adding ALL values)
Mark 3: $= 7\,104$ (1CA simplification — at least 6 values correct)
[Accept 7 136 = full marks.]
AO (answer only acceptable).

subQuestions.questionText: Write down the level descriptors which show that the performance of the Grade 11 learners is below the performance of the Grade 10 learners.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1–3: L2 (3RT correct level).
At L2, Grade 11 (1 990) is below Grade 10 (2 239), indicating fewer Grade 11 learners reached this level descriptor.

subQuestions.questionText: Determine the median level descriptor for the Grade 11 learners.
subQuestions.memoText:
(CA from Q5.1.4.)
Method 1:
Mark 1: Arrange Grade 11 values in order: $62; 223; 551; \mathbf{935}; 1\,231; 1\,357; 1\,990$ (1MCA arranging in order)
Mark 2: Median value = 935 (1CA correct median)
Mark 3: Median level descriptor = L4 (1CA level descriptor)

OR Method 2:
Mark 1: Arrange the level descriptors in increasing order of frequency: L7, L6, L5, L4, L3, L2, L1 → L4 is the middle (1MCA arranging)
Mark 2: Correct order (1CA)
Mark 3: Level descriptor = L4 (1CA)
AO (answer only acceptable).

subQuestions.questionText: The incomplete frequency table shows the Mathematical Literacy marks of a group of 67 learners. Complete the tally for the 70–79% interval.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1–2: ||||  | (i.e. five strokes plus one — representing 6) (2A correct tally).
Reasoning: Total is 67. Sum of known frequencies excluding 70–79: $0 + 3 + 12 + 7 + 15 + 17 + 4 + 2 + 1 = 61$. So 70–79 frequency $= 67 - 61 = 6$.

subQuestions.questionText: Write down the frequency for the 70–79% interval.
subQuestions.memoText:
(CA from Q5.2.1.)
Mark 1–2: 6 (2CA correct frequency).

subQuestions.questionText: Show, by means of calculations, how the cumulative frequency for the 30–39% interval was determined.
subQuestions.memoText:
Method 1:
Mark 1: $43 + 17$ (1RT correct values)
Mark 2: $= 60$ (1MA simplification)

OR Method 2:
Mark 1: $0 + 3 + 6 + 12 + 7 + 15 + 17$ (1RT correct values)
Mark 2: $= 60$ (1MA simplification)

subQuestions.questionText: (Refer to ANNEXURE C — graph showing the number of candidates who sat for the NSC Examinations in Mathematics, Technical Mathematics and Mathematical Literacy for the period 2014 to 2019.) Name the type of graph given in ANNEXURE C.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Stacked (1A stacked)
Mark 2: bar graph (1A bar graph)
Final answer: Stacked bar graph.

subQuestions.questionText: Write down, in words, the number of learners who sat for the Mathematical Literacy examination in 2018. (Value: 294 202.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Two hundred and ninety four thousand (1A first part of wording)
Mark 2: two hundred and two (1A second part of wording)
Full answer: Two hundred and ninety four thousand two hundred and two.

subQuestions.questionText: Determine how many more learners sat for Mathematical Literacy than for Mathematics and Technical Mathematics combined in 2019. (2019: Math Lit = 298 607; Mathematics = 222 034; Technical Mathematics = 9 670.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: $298\,607 - 222\,034 - 9\,670$ (1RT correct values)
Mark 2: (1M subtracting)
Mark 3: $= 66\,903$ (1CA simplification — two values must be correct)
AO (answer only acceptable).

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the mean number of learners doing Mathematics over the period shown (2014–2019). (Values: 2014 = 225 458; 2015 = 263 903; 2016 = 265 810; 2017 = 245 103; 2018 = 233 858; 2019 = 222 034.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Reading values from the graph (1RT correct values)
Mark 2: Mean $= \frac{225\,458 + 263\,903 + 265\,810 + 245\,103 + 233\,858 + 222\,034}{6}$ (1M concept of mean)
Mark 3: $= 242\,694{,}33$ (1CA simplification)
NPR.

subQuestions.questionText: Determine the range of the Mathematical Literacy learners over the period shown.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: $388\,845 - 294\,202$ (1MA concept of range)
Mark 2: $= 94\,643$ (1CA simplification — one value must be correct)

subQuestions.questionText: The total number of candidates doing the examinations in the three subjects in 2019 was 530 311. Calculate (rounded to ONE decimal place) the difference in the percentage of learners doing Mathematics instead of Mathematical Literacy in South Africa.
subQuestions.memoText:
Method 1:
Mark 1: Reading $222\,034$ and $298\,607$ (1RT correct values)
Mark 2: % for Mathematics $= \frac{222\,034}{530\,311} \times \frac{100}{1}$ (1MA percentage calculation)
Mark 3: $= 41{,}8686\%$ (1CA simplification)
Mark 4: % for Mathematical Literacy $= \frac{298\,607}{530\,311} \times \frac{100}{1} = 56{,}3079\%$ (1CA simplification)
Mark 5: Difference $= 56{,}3079\% - 41{,}8686\% = 14{,}4\%$ (1CA simplification with correct rounding)

OR Method 2:
Mark 1: Reading values (1RT correct values)
Mark 2: $298\,607 - 222\,034$ (1M subtracting values)
Mark 3: Denominator $= 530\,311$ (1CA correct denominator)
Mark 4: $\frac{298\,607 - 222\,034}{530\,311} \times 100$ (1MA percentage calculation)
Mark 5: $= 14{,}4\%$ (1CA simplification with correct rounding)
